attributes.parameters: Ridge logistic regression over 114 CADD input features, the GPN-MSA LLR and the Borzoi l2 of l2 scores; leave-one-chromosome-out
attributes.provenance_note: Section 6 'Model ensembling' defines the term: "we do see small improvements when ensembling CADD with a reduced number of features from other models (LLR for GPN-MSA and “ℓ2 of ℓ2 scores” for Borzoi), which we refer to as “lightweight” feature ensembling (Figure 8)". That composition is this record. The Table S11 caption says only "lightweight feature ensemble is evaluated for Mendelian traits" and does not repeat the composition; Figure 8 plots this ensemble alongside two smaller feature sets (CADD+GPN-MSA_LLR and CADD+Borzoi_L2_L2) and CADD alone, and this one scores highest.

attributes.value: Nine control variants are sampled for each putatively causal variant. attributes.source_locator: Table 3 and Section 5 (pages 6 to 7) and Appendix B.3 (pages 23 to 24)
attributes.value: Table 3 fixes what each class of model contributes. Functional-genomics-supervised models (Enformer, Borzoi) give l2 scores, the norm over spatial positions of the log2 fold change in predicted activity between the alternate and reference sequence, per track, plus their aggregation across tracks ('l2 of l2 scores', all tracks and within each assay type); the zero-shot score is the l2 of l2 over all tracks. Sei gives changes in sequence class scores, with the maximum absolute change as the zero-shot score. Self-supervised models give the log-likelihood ratio and its absolute value, and the embedding inner product for each hidden dimension, with the embedding inner product, l2 distance and cosine distance as zero-shot scores. The integrative model gives CADD input features and the CADD score, with the CADD score as the zero-shot score, and conservation scores are used directly. Predictions are always averaged over the forward and reverse strand for reverse-complement invariance.

attributes.value: The paper states that TraitGym was designed to have simple metrics and be tractable even for billion-parameter models, but has limited ability to resolve subtle differences in performance: the advantage of GPN-MSA over other alignment-based zero-shot scores on Mendelian traits is visible only on the expanded datasets. For deeper evaluation it recommends the genome-wide benchmarks of Benegas et al. (2025a), and for complex traits partitioned linkage disequilibrium score regression, which is not limited to fine-mapped or genome-wide-significant variants. The labels are curated pathogenic variants and fine-mapping output, not experimental measurements.

attributes.value: Table S8 prints the zero-shot AUPRC of ten genomic language models under five scoring approaches on both datasets, 100 cells, rounded to three decimal places. All 100 cells equal the corresponding value in the benchmark's own Hugging Face metric files, already in the store as 100 results from lit-genomics-20261011-traitgym-source-hf-metrics, when those full-precision values are rounded to three decimal places, with no disagreement. The two are on the same basis: Appendix B.4 states the weighted average over chromosomes is used for zero-shot scores as well, and the stored values come from the files under AUPRC_by_chrom_weighted_average/all/. The embedding columns correspond to the Embeddings.* metric files rather than to the six InnerProduct and EuclideanDistance files the benchmark also publishes for Mendelian traits. The printed value settles that mapping for one of the six: GPN-Promoter, L2 dist., Mendelian traits is 0.345, where GPN_final_Embeddings.plus.euclidean_distance is 0.3449957 and GPN_final_EuclideanDistance.plus.score is 0.3469633, which rounds to 0.347. For the other five, all Inner prod. cells, the two published files agree to three decimal places, so the printed value is consistent with either and the mapping rests on the column's name and on the Embeddings.* files being the set published for both datasets. The paper prints no value for the 36 stored linear probing results, which appear only in Figure 5, for the 14 stored zero-shot results of models that are not genomic language models, or for those 6 duplicate scoring variants. The cell-by-cell table is data/omics/traitgym-20261116/extract/comparison.tsv, produced by data/omics/traitgym-20261116/extract/compare_s8.py; the review re-did the comparison independently in data/omics/traitgym-20261116/review/reconcile-s8.tsv.

attributes.value: GPN-Promoter was trained on 512-bp sequences centred on the transcription start sites of protein-coding genes in reference genomes of animal species. Transcription start site coordinates came from NCBI Datasets gene annotations; species with gene annotations were subsampled to at most one per family, giving 434 reference genomes. The training objective follows GPN: base-pair-level tokenisation and masked language modelling of local 512-bp windows, with repeat positions, soft-masked in the reference genome, downweighted. It is trained only on promoters as an attempt to focus on regulatory regions; the paper says it would have liked to train on enhancers too but no annotation exists for non-model organisms.

attributes.source_locator: Table 2 (page 6), Appendix B.2 and Table S6 (pages 22 to 23)
attributes.value: The architecture follows ByteNet: blocks alternating dilated convolutions and feed-forward layers. Table S6 gives window size 512, repeat weight 0.01, embedding dimension 1024, slim True, 64 convolutional blocks, convolutional kernel size 9 in the first block and 5 in the remaining blocks, a dilation schedule of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 repeating, the AdamW optimizer, weight decay 0.01, batch size 2048, 370 K steps, learning rate 1e-3 and a 1 K step learning rate warmup. Table 2 gives 152M parameters, a context size of 512 and 1,026 extracted features. Training took approximately two weeks on four NVIDIA A100 40GB GPUs.
